headline: EPFO Approves Systematic Withdrawal Plan For Retirement Savings
metaDescription: The EPFO has approved a new Systematic Withdrawal Plan allowing retirees to receive predictable income while retaining ownership of their total corpus.
aiSummaryBullets: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation has approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan for retirement members.
This initiative allows retirees to convert savings into a predictable stream of income.
Members can now maintain ownership of their corpus instead of withdrawing the full amount within three years.
aiContextParagraph: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) recently approved the introduction of a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) to assist retirees in managing their funds. Currently, members are obligated to withdraw their entire provident fund corpus within a three-year window following retirement to prevent accounts from becoming inoperative and losing interest earnings. The newly approved policy changes this structure by allowing individuals to receive regular, predictable income streams from their savings. A key feature of this plan is that it enables members to retain ownership of their underlying corpus, providing more flexibility and stability in their post-retirement financial planning. This shift is intended to modernize how retirement savings are accessed, moving away from the previous requirement that forced a complete liquidation of the account shortly after leaving the workforce.
whyItIsViral: This development is being tracked by multiple national news outlets following the official announcement from the retirement fund regulatory body.
